## R Markdown


We start by loading our libraries  
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
```
# GOAL 
1. Extract a table of Guatemala City with age, population and sex and visual impairments
2. Obatin a summary of the population per zones
3. Obatin the density of population per zone 
4. Join the information to the zones shapefile 


Looking at the data types 
```{r}
# every text in na = c(...) is read as NA
censo_gt <- read_csv("training/training02/guatemala_subset.csv",
                             na = c("", "NA", "n/a", "N/A", "-"))
```
```{r}
censo_gt %>% head(10)
```

```{r}
names(censo_gt)
censo_gt %>% distinct(MUNICIPIO)
```

Selecting only the data for Guatemala City and only taking the columns of interest: 

PCP6 = Sex 
1 Hombre 
2 Mujer 


PCP7 = Age 


PCP16_A = Difficulty to see values from: 1-4 and 9 
1 No, sin dificultad
2 Sí, con algo de dificultad
3 Sí, con mucha dificultad
4 No puede
9 No declarado

```{r}
censo_ciudad <-  censo_gt %>% select(MUNICIPIO, LUGAR_POBLADO, NOMBRE_LUGAR_POBLADO, PCP6, PCP7, PCP16_A) %>%
  filter(MUNICIPIO == 101)

```


We are going to group by our zone to obtain the summary of statistics 

```{r}

censo_ciudad %>% distinct(NOMBRE_LUGAR_POBLADO)

```
Now we are going to obtain the summary of population per zone 
```{r}

population_summary <- censo_ciudad %>% group_by(NOMBRE_LUGAR_POBLADO) %>% summarise(Men = sum(PCP6 == 1), Women = sum(PCP6 == 2), Total_Pop = n()) %>% clean_names()

```

Now we want to extract the numbers from the text 
```{r}
population_summary<- population_summary %>% mutate(zona = str_remove(nombre_lugar_poblado, "Zona Municipal "))

population_summary <- population_summary %>% select(zona, nombre_lugar_poblado, men, women, total_pop)
```
